summary: This study compares an original vacuum-filtered Ti3C2Tx film with porous Ti3C2Tx films made by partial H2O2 oxidation followed by 3 M HCl etching. Eight distinct fabricated films were identified: the original control; C-0.05, C-0.1/T-40, C-0.15, and C-0.2 concentration variants; and T-20, T-30, T-60, and T-80 time variants. C-0.1 and T-40 are the same 0.1 M H2O2, 40 min material and therefore are consolidated into one electrode. The primary T-40 electrode delivered 385 F/g at 1 A/g in 1 M H2SO4 and had a BET area of 48.3 m2/g. Numerical capacitance values for the remaining variants are plotted but not printed; thickness, areal loading, porosity percentage, and numerical interlayer spacings are absent.
